Map.map_keyboard_help: Interactive map. With the map focused, use the arrow keys to pan and the plus and minus keys to zoom in and out. The same data is also available as tables and rankings on the analysis pages.
Map.scenario_fronteira_tip: Biogas Frontier: realistic-high mobilization of all 31 residues — surpasses the FIESP benchmark (~6.4 Mm³/d biomethane).
Map.scenario_real_tip: Real Scenario (CP2b N4, accessible potential): the mobilisable potential (N3) after storage losses and the spatial logistic factor computed on the road network (hubs that reach a viable scale). The full factor cascade of the CP2b v5.1 method, reference scenario. SP: 16.4 Mm³/day of CH₄ (min–max scenario envelope 5.2–42.7, not a probability interval). 11 of 17 substrates still carry provisional parameters.
Map.scenario_ideal_tip: Ideal Scenario (CP2b N3, mobilisable potential): technical potential minus uses that exclude digestion and the methane operating plants already recover, before storage losses and logistics. The CP2b v5.1 headline figure, reference scenario. SP: 19.2 Mm³/day of CH₄ (min–max scenario envelope 7.7–45.0); sugarcane includes surplus bagasse. 11 of 17 substrates still carry provisional parameters.
Map.scenario_served_note: Real and Ideal scenarios (CP2b method) are available for São Paulo only.

metadata.description: Open platform that estimates, municipality by municipality, the biogas and bioproduct potential of agricultural, livestock and urban residues. Interactive map, multi-criteria analysis and methane potential by residue and municipality; availability factors under review.

what.a: An open platform, developed at NIPE/UNICAMP, that estimates, municipality by municipality, the biogas and bioproduct potential of agricultural, livestock and urban residues. The <guide>guide</guide> shows the first steps.

coverage.q: Which regions does the platform cover?
coverage.a: São Paulo state is the canonical base, with every layer and analysis. Minas Gerais is a pilot, marked “beta — in validation”: its figures may still change. Expansion to the rest of Brazil is under way.

potential.q: What are theoretical and available potential?
potential.a: Theoretical potential starts from the amount of residue generated. Available potential applies availability factors per residue, which estimate the share that can actually be mobilised and are under review. References and chemical characterization are in the <science>Scientific Database</science>.

reuse.q: Can I reuse the data and the code?
reuse.a: Yes. The code is licensed under GPL-3.0 and the data under CC BY 4.0, which allows any use, commercial included, as long as the source is credited. See <cite>How to cite</cite>.

accessibility.a: The goal is WCAG 2.1 level AA: keyboard navigation, text alternatives and sufficient contrast. The <a11y>accessibility statement</a11y> describes the current state and how to report barriers.

report.q: I found an error in the data. How do I report it?
report.a: Write to the team through the <contact>contact channels</contact> on this page, naming the municipality, the indicator and the screen where you saw it.

mapa.title: Interactive Map
mapa.subtitle: Visually explore the biogas potential in each municipality of São Paulo.

sections.title: What is it
sections.content:
The Interactive Map presents the geographic distribution of the estimated production potential of biomass, biogas, biomethane, and bioenergy from urban, livestock, agricultural, or forestry organic waste across the municipalities of the State of São Paulo (canonical base) and, as a beta in validation, those of Minas Gerais, with options for total and per capita potential. The displayed potential is broken down by the source of each part of the total potential, distinguishing across all waste classes.
 In addition to potential, the tool allows visualizing the infrastructure of the State of São Paulo (biogas plants, ethanol mills, electrical substations, etc.), logistics elements, and site constraints.

sections.title: What is it for
How to use
sections.content:
1. With the map open, look at the sidebar on the left side of the screen featuring all available analysis filters and select your preferences.
2. Select the municipality in the top search bar or click directly on it in the map.
3. View the generation indicators in the right sidebar, containing an overview, potential, waste breakdown, and a button for a more detailed municipal analysis.

analises.title: Advanced Analyses
analises.subtitle: Explore the possible filters and get the simulations of biogas potential from different scenarios.

sections.title: What is it
sections.content:
The Advanced Analyses section allows modeling detailed biogas production estimates. By selecting waste types, sub-residues, and scenarios (baseline, conservative, optimistic, or biogas frontier), the platform calculates and displays theoretical potential, losses at each stage, and final real potential.
All parameters are customizable: users can adjust harvest, competition, seasonality, and logistics factors, as well as inspect the mathematical formulas applied directly on the page.

sections.title: What is it for
How to use

base-cientifica.title: Scientific Basis
base-cientifica.subtitle: Visually explore the scientific foundations supporting the platform's results and potentials.

sections.title: What is it
sections.content:
The Scientific Knowledge Base brings together the articles and technical reports supporting the platform's data. Each metric used in potential calculations is grounded in auditable bibliographic references available for direct consultation.
In addition, the section features two comparative analysis tools among the residues studied in PILAR-2b:
• Degradation Curves: analysis of methane production kinetics over time.
• Multi-parameter Comparison: direct contrast between key indicators, such as BMP, C:N, VS, and CH₄ content.

sections.title: What is it for
sections.content:
• Ensure transparency and methodological rigor: confirms the scientific sources supporting the final potential calculation.
• Support new research: serves as a structured database for advanced studies in biogas and bioproducts.
• Streamline comparative diagnostics: allows evaluating the performance and physicochemical characteristics of different waste types.

sections.title: How to use
sections.content:
1. Explore References: On the main screen, select one of the 40 residues distributed across 4 economic sectors to access the 'Chemical Characterization' section and view its bibliographic references.
2. Analyze Degradation Kinetics: Access the 'Degradation Kinetics' tab, select up to 6 residues simultaneously, and view methane production behavior over days.
3. Make Direct Comparisons: In the 'Interactive Comparison' tab, cross-reference multiple operational and chemical parameters among the selected residues.

calculadora.title: Biogas Calculator
calculadora.subtitle: Calculate the implementation feasibility of a biogas and bioproducts project.

sections.title: What is it
sections.content: The Biogas Calculator is a tool designed for users seeking to valorize biomass residues for bioenergy and bioproduct generation. In the initial form, the user enters the residue type, the annual volume generated (in tons per year or by cultivation area in hectares), the harvest period (seasonality months), and the final product of interest. From these inputs, the platform projects biogas potential (in m³/year), allows configuring the system implementation level, and provides an estimated financial return (payback).

sections.title: What is it for
How to use

proximidade.title: Proximity Analysis
proximidade.subtitle: Spatial and logistical simulation by catchment radius for biogas and biomethane plant feasibility.

sections.title: What is it
sections.content:
Proximity Analysis is a geospatial tool that allows selecting any coordinate in the State of São Paulo and defining a customizable catchment radius (buffer from 10 km to 100 km).
The tool automatically aggregates all municipalities within the area of influence, calculating the total analyzed area, agricultural area, and primary class, while detailing land use distribution and providing feedback on biogas production suitability.

sections.title: What is it for
sections.content:
• Evaluate locational feasibility and optimal economic radius for biomass transport for the installation of biogas and biomethane plants.
• Identify neighboring municipalities for regional consortium formation.
• Analyze surrounding land suitability (detailed land use breakdown) for continuous substrate supply.

sections.title: How to use
sections.content:
1. Click anywhere on the interactive map to define the point of interest (latitude and longitude).
2. Adjust the "Catchment Radius" slider (from 10 km to 100 km), following the logistics feasibility recommendations.
3. Click the "Analyze" button to process spatial data.
4. Explore results: agricultural area, detailed MapBiomas class distribution, and energy indicators.
5. Use the "Export Data" button to download the CSV spreadsheet or "Share" to generate a direct link with the analyzed coordinate and radius.

notes.heading: Notes and limitations
items: The potential is a model estimate, built from official data on crop production, herds, population and sanitation. It is not a field measurement.
The values are methane (CH₄). Raw biogas also contains other gases, so the same potential as biogas is a larger volume.
The accessible level (N4) accounts for logistics to a plant of viable scale. A municipality can have mobilisable potential (N3) and zero accessible potential when no plant reaches that scale.
The method covers the municipalities of São Paulo. Those in other states show as no CP2b data.

overview.title: How PILAR-2b calculates potential
overview.lede: Every figure on the platform starts from official data, goes through four availability factors and ends as biogas potential. These pages show each step, with its sources and its confidence.
overview.fde_formula_note: The FDE is the share of the residue generated that reaches a biogas plant. It is never stored: it is always computed from the four factors.
overview.potential_formula_note: Generation comes from official sources per municipality; the BMP (methane potential) comes from the science base, per residue.
overview.licence: Code GPL-3.0 · Data and documentation CC BY 4.0.

fde.title: Availability factors (FDE)
fde.lede: Not every residue generated becomes biogas. Four factors take the amount generated down to the amount available, and each residue has its own.
fde.competition_note: FCp enters as (1 − FCp): it is the share that goes to other uses, so what is left for biogas is the complement.
fde.table_caption: Each residue's collection, competition, seasonality and logistics factors, the resulting FDE and the confidence level
fde.bands_lede: Each residue carries a confidence level, which says where its factors come from and how far the figure can vary.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.lede: The map shows two scenarios. The chemistry is the same in both; what changes is how much of the residue reaches a digester.
scenarios.real_body: The residue that actually reaches a digester today, with current collection rates and competing uses. It is the scenario the map opens on.
scenarios.ideal_body: All the residue generated is collected and treated. It is an infrastructure hypothesis: it shows the ceiling, not a forecast.
scenarios.definitions: The definitions follow the Atlas de Bioenergia SP 2020. Both scenarios are computed on the server, and every coefficient is recorded and auditable.
scenarios.ch4_body: Methane is taken as {share} of raw biogas (FIESP 2025), the same value on the server and in the browser.
scenarios.retired_body: Earlier versions offered four band scenarios (conservative, medium term, frontier and optimistic), which moved the BMP within its uncertainty range. They left the map because they answer how much the chemistry could yield, not how much residue reaches a digester. Old links with those scenarios still open.
scenarios.map_cta: See the scenarios on the map

validation.title: Validation and limitations
validation.lede: What backs each factor, how far it can vary and what the data does not say yet.

process.data: Production: official data (IBGE, EMBRAPA, UNICA) where it exists; sector reports where it does not, with lower confidence.
process.competition: Competing uses: each alternative destination (cogeneration, fertilizer, feed, industrial use) and the legal requirements, such as fertigation regulated by CETESB.
process.collection: Collection, seasonality and logistics: how concentrated or dispersed the source is, transport and storage infrastructure, and the production calendar.
process.conservative: Where the evidence is uncertain, the factor takes the conservative estimate and the residue gets low confidence.

validation.beta: The database is in beta: the factors are still being validated, and each correction is published in the patch notes.
validation.report_body: Write to the team: name the residue, the municipality or the page, and what looks wrong.
